title: Low-Cal Haloumi San Choy Bau
subtitle: with Capsicum and Crunchy Cashews
description: Our veggie version of san choy bau features carrot, capsicum and spring onion topped with pan-fried chunks of haloumi. Pile into lettuce cups, add cashews for crunch, then dig in!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Thinly slice the capsicum and spring onion. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Peel the carrot, then shred using a julienne peeler or coarsely grate with a box grater. Cut the haloumi into 2cm chunks and put in a bowl. Add the Chinese barbecue seasoning and toss to coat. Coarsely chop the cashews.

Prep lettuce: Trim the base of the lettuce, then separate the leaves and rinse under cold water. Pat dry with paper towel. Reserve two-thirds of the largest lettuce cups, then thinly slice the remaining lettuce (see Make it yours).

Stir-fry veggies: Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in a medium frypan over medium heat. Stir-fry the capsicum for 3 mins or until starting to soften. Add the spring onion, carrot and garlic and stir-fry for 1-2 mins until tender. Remove from the pan.

Pan-fry haloumi: Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in the same pan over medium-high heat. Cook the haloumi, stirring, for 1 min or until golden. Add 1 tbs soy sauce, 1½ tsp honey and 1 tbs water and cook, stirring, for 30-40 secs until the haloumi is sticky and the sauce is slightly reduced. Remove the pan from the heat.
Serve up: Divide the lettuce cups among plates. Top with the shredded lettuce, veggie mixture and haloumi. Scatter over the cashews and enjoy!

Make it yours: We like the fun of eating with our hands, but if you don't feel like getting your hands dirty, just thinly slice all the lettuce, pile all the ingredients into a bowl and serve as a salad.
